title: How do Soong, Kati and ninja split the work in one m?

glossary.full: A GNU make clone that emits Ninja files
glossary.note: Reads Android.mk and the product config.

glossary.full: The build conductor that runs Soong, Kati and Ninja

key_points: m starts soong_ui, which runs Soong and Kati and then one Ninja.
Soong reads Android.bp; Kati reads Android.mk and the product config.
soong_ui writes a combined Ninja file that includes both generated files.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Rookie types one letter, m, and hits Enter. A whole Android build starts. Who actually does the work?
beats.say: Rookie types one letter, em, and hits Enter. A whole Android build starts. Who actually does the work?

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: Isn't m just a shell function? What does it call?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: It runs build/soong/soong_ui.bash in make mode. That starts soong_ui, the conductor.
beats.say: It runs build slash soong slash soong underscore U I dot bash in make mode. That starts soong underscore U I, the conductor.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: First player: Soong. It reads every Android.bp and writes out/soong/build.ninja.
beats.say: First player: Soong. It reads every Android dot B P and writes out slash soong slash build dot ninja.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.say: And the old Android dot M K files?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: Kati reads those with the product config. It's a GNU make clone that writes a second Ninja file.
beats.say: Kati reads those with the product config. It's a G N U make clone that writes a second Ninja file.

beats.speaker: rookie
beats.text: Two Ninja files. Do they fight?

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: No. soong_ui writes one combined file that includes both.
beats.say: No. soong underscore U I writes one combined file that includes both.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: They even talk. Soong writes a makefile of its own, which Kati includes, so make's image rules can package Soong modules.

beats.speaker: senior
beats.text: One Ninja process. It runs the real compiler commands across the whole merged graph.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The results land under out/target/product, in a folder named for the device.
beats.say: The results land under out slash target slash product, in a folder named for the device.
